answer: Let a fresh identity first wander through a randomized challenge maze, so the path it traces becomes an unforgeable behavioral fingerprint. Then encode each epoch's answer as a sonnet-like rhythmic checksum, a persona signature tied to that identity. Finally, the network threads all signatures onto a trellis graph and runs community detection, so a cluster of clones shows up as a dense knot. An attacker must forge many maze-paths and sonnet checksums at once to climb the trellis, and both are anchored in real compute, so sybil cost grows superlinearly with each fake identity.
